_comment: VENUE-FACT CORRECTIONS FOR THE LLM-WRITTEN 'why' BLURBS. Added 2026-09-01 (DLR: 'some of the Auditorio Benalmadena information is still wrong'). WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the card blurbs are written by the weekly LLM sweep in all 8 languages and REGENERATE EVERY MONDAY, so a wrong fact about a venue cannot be fixed by editing a calendar row — it comes straight back. This is the same problem, and the same remedy, as the _house_en 'the Costa del Sol' stripper already in build_site.py: correct it at the OUTPUT BOUNDARY, on every build, where it can never come back. Applied per row in build_site.py immediately after the 'why' blurbs are read and next to the venue_time_override call, so it covers every page the blurb appears on and every language. SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY NARROW: a fix only runs when its venue_match is a substring of the row's normalised venue, and each rule is a literal-ish regex aimed at one wrong phrase — this is a FACT corrector, not a style rewriter. Do not use it to reword blurbs you merely dislike; fix those at source in source_calendar.py.

fixes.why: THE VENUE IS NOT ON THE SEAFRONT. The Auditorio Municipal de Benalmádena (programmed as Ópera Benalmádena, ticketed via tickets.oneboxtds.com/operabenalmadena) is at Avda de Rocío Jurado 0, ARROYO DE LA MIEL — the inland district, beside Parque de la Paloma, about a kilometre from the shore. Address confirmed 2026-09-01 from the venue's own site (operabenalmadena.com) and the Junta de Andalucía / Bandsintown venue records, which give the same Av. de Rocío Jurado 0, 29631 Arroyo de la Miel. The sweep nevertheless described it as a coastal / seafront / seaside auditorium in EVERY language — and the Nordic blurbs went further and put it on Benalmádenas STRANDPROMENAD(E), the beach promenade, which is a different place entirely. The site's own Benalmádena area copy already says 'the Auditorio's tribute, opera and zarzuela season in Arroyo de la Miel', so the blurbs also contradicted the page they sat on. 'Open-air' is CORRECT and is deliberately preserved by these rules — it is a genuine open-air auditorium; only the sea claim is removed.

NAME THE TRIBUTE ACTS. Added 2026-09-07 (Sofia). Three Benalmádena bills are sold on named tribute acts, but the sweep wrote the blurbs as 'con varios artistas' / 'across multiple acts' / 'med flera artister' — unsearchable, and useless to a reader deciding which of two consecutive nights to buy. source_calendar.py's MULTI-ACT BILLS rule is supposed to carry the names in `act` (and BLURB_SYSTEM would then inherit them), but the 2026-09-07 sweep did NOT apply it — the ticketer that names the acts is behind Cloudflare, and an LLM instruction is not a guarantee. These rules correct the prose deterministically until the rename lands. LINE-UPS VERIFIED 2026-09-06 on the seller's own INFORMACIÓN tab (Sofia's browser): 'FESTIVAL DE ROCK – 12 Y 13 DE SEPTIEMBRE. Dos noches. Cuatro leyendas.' / '12 DE SEPTIEMBRE: LED ZEPPELIN & KISS' / '13 DE SEPTIEMBRE: BON JOVI & AC/DC'; and for 20 Sep, 'tres de los artistas más importantes de la historia del country: Shania Twain, Dolly Parton y Kenny Rogers'. PATTERNS ARE DELIBERATELY LONG: 'con varios artistas' alone would also fire on Legends Night (3 Oct) and Rock & Pop Legends (16 Oct) at this same venue and name the wrong bands, so each pattern carries enough of its own sentence to be unique to that event. A rule that stops matching after a future sweep simply does not fire — it cannot corrupt a blurb.

fixes.why: ZZ PUB HAS A DOOR COVER (€10/€15) — NOT free (DLR 2026-09-08). Every ZZ Pub night shows a small '€10/€15 cover' price pill + 'Check venue' (never 'Free'/'Free info'). Poster-verified below. Every sweep writes the ZZ Pub nights as free — 'Música en vivo gratuita', 'Free live music', 'Kostenlose Live-Musik' — in all eight languages, and it is wrong in all eight. ZZ Pub's own September poster, quoted verbatim on zzpub.es/conciertos-en-malaga-septiembre-2026/, reads: 'Aforo limitado. Ocupar tu aforo 10€, excepto viernes y sábado 15€. Regalo 1 copa o 2 cervezas.' So entry is 10€ Sunday-Thursday and 15€ Friday and Saturday, each including a drink or two beers. Telling readers a paid night is free is the one error that makes someone turn up and be refused at the door. THESE RULES ONLY STRIP THE FALSE CLAIM — they deliberately do NOT write a number into the blurb, because a single venue-wide rule cannot know which day a row falls on, and a flat '10€' would be wrong on the six Friday/Saturday dates still to come this month (11, 12, 18, 19, 25, 26 Sep). The price belongs in the card's own price pill, which is driven by the row's `free` flag, NOT here. Swedish and Danish share the identical opening 'Gratis livemusik' and take the same replacement, which is harmless since the corrected word is identical in both.
